title: Recovery of a torsor-trivialized finite-ring module sheaf
statement: Let X be a connected scheme, R a finite commutative ring, P a finite group, c:Y→X a connected finite etale ULift(P)-torsor, F a sheaf of R-modules on X_et and A an R-module. If c*F is isomorphic to the constant sheaf A, then some R-linear P-representation M has T_c(M) isomorphic to F, where T_c is the explicit functor of [def-weil-pbc-finite-ring-torsor-associated-module]. No filtration or Sylow assertion is part of this statement.

source.place: Tags 0DV5 (3) and 0DV6; sites.tex Tags 04TR and 04TS, equivariant sections and descent along the given torsor

proof.text: Construct M=F(Y), with g acting by restriction along the inverse deck transformation. The contravariance and deck multiplication equations prove that this is an R-linear representation. No object is chosen from an unproved existence theorem.

Use the module-valued locally constant comparison for the supplied trivialization of c*F. Connectedness and nonemptiness of Y identify A linearly with F(Y). Restrict a section over W to W×_X Y and read it as a locally constant F(Y)-valued function β_W. This is R-linear, natural in W, and normalized on the diagonal. All linearity is retained in ModuleCat, rather than inferred from additivity.

On an object with a map f to Y, constant coordinates identify sections with locally constant functions valued in F(Y). Restricting to an open fibre gives a local constant presentation. Naturality and diagonal normalization then show evaluation on the graph of f is this bijection. These local presentations also prove β_W(s)(g*x)=F(g inverse)(β_W(s)(x)), so β takes values in the equivariant section presheaf.

An equivariant function is determined by its values on the graph of a torsor section, because its P-translates cover the fibre product. Combining this injectivity with graph evaluation bijectivity shows the normalized evaluation α is bijective on every object admitting a map to Y. Every W is etale-covered by W×_X Y, so α is locally injective and locally surjective. Sheafification inverts α. Compose its inverse with the sheafification counit for F to obtain T_c(M)≅F. Empty objects, the zero ring and the identity torsor obey the same formulas.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteRing_module_descent
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace X]
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    (P : Type u) [Group P] [Finite P]
    (c : Scheme.GaloisCover (ULift.{u + 1} P) X) [ConnectedSpace c.P]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (A : ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)
    (hF : Nonempty ((Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) c.π).obj F ≅
      (constantSheaf c.P.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj A)) :
    ∃ M : Rep.{u + 1} Λ P,
      Nonempty ((c.associatedModuleFunctorOver Λ).obj M ≅ F)
